answer: To compare candidate checkouts fairly, hold every scenario input constant except the candidate configuration: the same workload (same arrival process and rate, Poisson at 20 requests per second, same 1,800-second horizon and 300-second warmup), the same metric identifiers, units and definitions, the same seed base and deterministic seed = base + replication scheme, and the same hard constraints. Only the candidate configuration (server count, service-time distribution, queue capacity, timeout, retry budget, bulkhead and unit cost) is the intended experimental variable; giving one candidate a shorter warmup or a lower arrival rate invalidates the comparison, and a genuinely different workload must be declared as part of that candidate.
